Karthik —

Thanks for circling back. Two items from our side that block legal: 1) we want a clear mechanism so that if NovaMed is required to produce evidence (logs, model prompts) in response to a third-party claim, the MSA names a single technical custodian and a single legal contact for preservation requests; 2) we want the handback process defined if Redwood takes over defense — specifically, timelines and what is returned to NovaMed after matter resolution (redacted or full bundles).

Can your team propose language? Our outside counsel (Erin) is copied. We prefer to avoid a lengthy escrow if we can map responsibilities operationally.

Matt

Matt —

Appreciate the clarity. Quick answers while legal drafts language:
- We can name a single Evidence Custodian (platform-ops@redwood.com) and a single Legal Contact (legal-notices@redwood.com) in the Order Form.
- Redwood is comfortable defining a handback window (30 days after final settlement or dismissal) for returning copies of evidence we retained while defending, with limited redaction rights to preserve privilege.
- We prefer operational handoff over full escrow in many cases; if NovaMed needs escrow for particularly sensitive artifacts we can discuss an addendum.

Looping in Kim and Ben to work the redline. Kim — can you draft two short clauses: (A) Notice & Preservation Custodian naming + SLA for initial preservation response (48 hours); (B) Evidence Custody & Handback: what Redwood returns, timeline, privilege carveout language, and an optional escrow trigger if preservation includes raw training data.

Ben — heads-up for deal team; there may be a small delay while we finalize the language, but this is standard.

Thanks,
Karthik

Subject: RE: MSA + Order Form: litigation custodian & evidence-handback mechanics

Matt / Erin / Karthik —

Attached are two proposed short clauses intended to slot into the MSA (and referenced in the Order Form):

1) Evidence Preservation & Custodian
"Upon receipt of a third-party claim alleging intellectual property infringement, Customer shall notify Redwood and designate a single Evidence Custodian (the \"Custodian\") for technical artifact preservation. Redwood will designate a single Redwood Custodian for operational requests. Each party will acknowledge receipt within forty-eight (48) hours and begin preservation steps as described in the Evidence Matrix. Initial preservation is limited to runtime logs, prompt/response bundles, and metadata necessary to investigate the claim."

2) Custody During Defense and Handback
"If Redwood assumes defense under the MSA, Redwood will secure and retain copies of preserved materials. Following final resolution (dismissal, settlement, or judgment), Redwood will return non-privileged copies of preserved materials to Customer within thirty (30) days. Redwood will redact materials to protect Redwood privileged communications and third-party confidential information. If preserved materials include raw customer training datasets, the parties will follow the Escrow Trigger process set out in Appendix C to determine whether escrowing or secure return is required."

Notes / operational points:
- SLA: initial acknowledgement 48 hours; full evidence delivery plan within 7 business days
- We should include an "Escrow Trigger" threshold (e.g., >100GB of raw customer-supplied data or inclusion of third-party confidential datasets) to avoid escrow for common cases
- Insurance/indemnity interplay: if defense is taken by Redwood, standard cooperation obligations remain and Redwood will not waive subrogation claims without Customer consent

Matt / Erin — please flag any specific language you need changed. Happy to tighten redactions vs. return matrix.

Regards,
Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel | Redwood Inference

Kim / Karthik —

Thanks — the proposed clauses look reasonable and concise. A couple of small asks from NovaMed counsel: 1) can we make the 30-day handback optional where regulators or court orders require longer retention; 2) please expand the initial preservation list to include (a) policy snapshots (config state), (b) any feature flags in effect at time of alleged incident, and (c) the exact model variant + quantization profile. Those three items are critical for our internal forensic review.

Erin, can you confirm if the additional items are standard practice? If so, we'll accept with a small note on regulatory exceptions for the handback timeline.

If we have agreement on these points we can sign-off on the redline and proceed to final procurement pricing.

Matt
